raw_response:
I am getting older, so this year I will not do anything fancy. On my 10.1 mu I will still keep the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the safest way for my family. Wheat gives a steady crop, and maize after wheat makes full use of the land. I watch what men around my village do, and most years this way is still the most reliable. If I change too much and it goes wrong, at my age that loss is hard to make back.

For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, not too early and not too late. I will use a common improved local seed that people nearby have been using, because saved seed is cheaper but the stand is not as even. I cannot spend wildly, but I also do not want the wheat to look weak, so I will put a fair base fertilizer and then topdress once around jointing if the crop looks all right. Since I have well water, I plan about three irrigations for wheat, but if spring rain is decent, I may save one to cut pumping cost. For maize, I have to move fast after wheat harvest. The time is tight, so I will use simple rotary tillage or even direct sow right after wheat if I can get it done quickly. I will use hybrid maize seed like my neighbors do. Maize I usually feed enough fertilizer to keep the leaves dark and the ears full, but not so much that I spend all my cash on inputs. If summer rain is normal, one irrigation is enough; if it turns dry at tasseling, I will add another if I can afford the pumping.
